root_cause.text: Race condition where `wbt_enable_default()` (which includes `wbt_init()` initialization of the inflight counter) is called concurrently with IO submission, allowing the inflight counter to be decremented before proper initialization completes, leading to a negative counter and hung tasks in `wbt_wait()`.

candidates.rationale: This statement sets the QUEUE_FLAG_REGISTERED flag, which allows I/O submission to proceed. Placing it before wbt_enable_default() creates a window where I/O can decrement the inflight counter before it is initialized by wbt_init(), leading to a negative count and potentially hanging tasks in wbt_wait().

This is the call to wbt_enable_default() that triggers wbt_init() to initialize the inflight counter. Because it is called after the queue is marked as registered, I/O can already be in flight, causing a race condition where the counter is decremented before initialization completes.

This check inside wbt_enable_default() tests whether the queue is registered, but due to the ordering in the caller, the queue is already registered when wbt_enable_default() is called. The check passes, allowing wbt_init() to run after I/O has already started, which is the core of the race.

This condition gates the call to wbt_init(). If it evaluates true (as it does for multiqueue devices with wbt enabled), wbt_init() is executed. The race arises because this initialization happens after the queue is already accepting I/O, leaving the inflight counter uninitialized during I/O submission.

This is the direct call to wbt_init() that initializes the inflight counter (among other wbt structures). If called too late (after I/O has started), the counter is zero or uninitialized when I/O decrements it, causing it to become negative and leading to hung tasks in wbt_wait().

This conditional checks whether wbt should be enabled after an elevator switch. If true, it calls wbt_enable_default(), which may race with I/O submissions that started before the new elevator is fully set up, potentially before the inflight counter is initialized.

This call site for wbt_enable_default() occurs after the elevator has been unregistered and the new elevator is about to be registered, but I/O might already be in flight due to the previous elevator. The inflight counter may not be initialized yet, causing a race condition similar to the sysfs path.
